title: Retrospective Analysis of Prognostic Clinical, Pathological, and Treatment-Related Factors and Their Impact on Overall Survival and Recurrence-Free Survival in Patients with Esophageal and Gastric Cancer, Including Adenocarcinomas of the Esophagogastric Junction (AEG)
summary:
Background
Cancer of the esophagus and stomach are among the most common cancers affecting the digestive system. Treatment options have improved considerably over recent years. However, outcomes and survival rates still vary substantially between patients. It is therefore important to better understand which patient-related, disease-related, and treatment-related factors are associated with more favorable or less favorable outcomes.
Research Question
The aim of this study is to investigate which factors influence disease progression and survival in people with cancer of the esophagus, stomach, or the area where the esophagus joins the stomach. In addition, the study seeks to determine whether treatment outcomes have changed over time and which treatment approaches are associated with better results.
Methods
This study will analyze existing medical records and follow-up data from patients who received treatment between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025. No additional examinations will be performed, and participation in the study will not affect patient care or treatment.
The analysis will include information such as age, sex, other health conditions, characteristics of the disease, type of treatment received, and subsequent disease course. Particular attention will be given to how long patients survive after treatment and how long they remain free from a return of the disease. Different treatment approaches will also be compared, and the relationship between treatment-related complications and long-term outcomes will be evaluated.
The results of this study may help improve future care for people with cancer of the esophagus and stomach by identifying factors that contribute to better outcomes and by supporting more individualized treatment strategies.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Histologically confirmed esophageal carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, or adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction.
- Treatment at the participating institution between January 1, 2010, and December 31, 2025.
- Availability of sufficient clinical, pathological, treatment-related, and follow-up data for analysis.
- Age ≥ 18 years at the time of diagnosis.
Exclusion criteria:
- Lack of histological confirmation of esophageal carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, or adenocarcinoma of the esophagogastric junction.
- Age < 18 years at the time of initial diagnosis.
- No curative-intent surgical resection of the primary tumor.
- Incomplete clinical, pathological, or treatment-related baseline data preventing adequate assessment of the study objectives.
- Missing or insufficient follow-up data for the evaluation of overall survival and/or disease-free survival.
- Presence of other malignant diseases that may substantially interfere with the assessment of the study-specific endpoints.
- Patients diagnosed and treated exclusively outside the study institution for whom adequate data are not available.
